A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and can be matched despite reformatting, relocation, and renumbering.

before.justification: v2 reports original quadrotor and MuJoCo experiments in Section 4, plus fighter-jet and nonlinear temperature-control simulations in Appendix B.

after.justification: v3 retains original control experiments and reports expanded MuJoCo evaluations, including data-size and data-quality studies in Appendix B.1.

M1.justification: v3 reports RBF/Gaussian state-feature variants for the MuJoCo IO policy, extending v2's listed history, cross-product, bias, and sinusoidal features (Section 4.2, Table 4). Algorithm 1, the suboptimality loss, and the robust-MPC distillation procedure remain unchanged.

E1.justification: v3 adds walker2d-expert data alongside walker2d-medium in Table 6, extending coverage to higher-quality demonstrations. Existing hopper/walker2d-medium, quadrotor, fighter-jet, and temperature-control coverage is retained. Additional subset sizes concern evaluation settings rather than new tasks.

E2.justification: The MuJoCo comparisons retain CQL, IQL, and COMBO and add MOPO and TD3BC, together with a training-dataset return reference (v3 Tables 1–2). Comparators in the quadrotor and other control experiments are unchanged.

E3.justification: v2 reports averages of the top 5% evaluation scores after a stated uniform one-million-update budget. v3 reports final and best epochs, introduces algorithm/configuration-dependent budgets and uniformly sampled subset experiments, and uses different walker2d-10K IO configurations for final versus best scores. Some budget and RBF descriptions conflict with Table 4, but the substantial protocol revision is clear.

E4.justification: New Appendix B.1 systematically examines IO performance across uniformly sampled dataset sizes, medium versus expert demonstrations, and training trajectories (Tables 5–6, Figure 3). These add substantial evidence about sample dependence and training stability. Earlier control robustness and feature/lookback analyses are retained, including the renumbered Sections B.2–B.3.

E5.justification: The reported MuJoCo training-seed count changes from three to four. v3 explicitly identifies table uncertainties as standard deviations and adds individual-seed learning curves. Forty evaluation seeds and the existing control experiments' trial and percentile reporting are retained.

E6.justification: MuJoCo results are substantially replaced and expanded. v2 Table 1 ranks IO first on both low-data tasks; under v3's revised best-epoch protocol, IQL leads hopper-5K (90.5 versus IO's 83.8), and COMBO leads walker2d-10K (76.3 versus 72.1). These are not comparisons under identical settings. v3 also adds final-epoch results, previously absent full-data IO scores, sensitivity results, and training times, while revising parameter counts.

T1.justification: Equation 12 in Theorem 3.3 restores the omitted quadratic control-cost term. That term already appeared in v2's underlying MPC objective, SDP reformulation, and Appendix A proof, so this corrects the stated mathematical equivalence. The lemmas and proofs otherwise retain their substance.

C1.justification: The conclusion replaces the MuJoCo SOTA claim with teacher-level recovery and competitive low-data performance. The abstract likewise emphasizes teacher recovery and drops the specific three-orders-of-magnitude parameter claim. Core methodological contributions persist, and Section 1.1 still retains its low-data SOTA wording.

C2.justification: New Remarks 2.4 and 3.6 discuss nonlinear feature/kernel expressiveness and dataset-dependent SDP scalability. Section 4.2 explains teacher-level performance through the absence of action improvement, while Appendix B.1 interprets the larger expert-data final/best gap through possible overfitting. Earlier nominal-model and counterfactual-disturbance limitations remain.

D1.justification: v3 adds a project code URL where v2 only promised an open-source package. It also supplies IO epochs, learning rates, decay factors, and RBF settings in Table 4, specifies dataset-subset selection, and reports RTX 3090 timing information in Table 3. Reproduction documentation expands substantially, although some budget and feature descriptions are inconsistent.

R1.justification: v3 adds Jacot et al. (2018), Long et al. (2024), and Zattoni Scroccaro et al. (2025) to support kernelization and scalable IO optimization discussions. The principal related-work discussion is retained; reference reordering and publication-metadata updates do not constitute additional research coverage.

P1.justification: v3 selectively expands the introduction, adds explanatory remarks, and rewrites parts of the MuJoCo discussion and conclusion. It inserts Appendix B.1, moves references after the appendices, and updates author information and acknowledgements. The main section sequence and much of the prose remain intact.

P2.justification: v3 adopts a substantially different TMLR layout, including the title/author block, headers, typography, and denser page composition. The combined MuJoCo table becomes separate final-score, best-score, and resource tables; three appendix tables and a four-panel learning-curve figure are added. Existing control plots are retained and relocated or renumbered.

improvement.justification: v3 substantially strengthens the evidence behind the MuJoCo claims: v2 relied on selected top-5% scores and omitted full-data IO results, whereas v3 supplies final and best scores, teacher references, learning curves, and targeted data-size/quality analyses. The more qualified conclusion, objective correction, and expanded reproduction details improve accuracy and transparency. Conflicting budget/RBF descriptions and retained SOTA wording remain weaknesses, but the overall evidential improvement is substantial.
